guard: x54-wrapper-cost: `_cs_isinv` resumes its walk from a saved point that is always a suffix of `_CS_TAIL`, instead of re-walking the tail once per quoted run
guard_site: lib/templates.py, the shared header - `_cs_isinv`'s seed and its two `_lastw=1` resume writes, plus the `_CS_INVPEND`/`_CS_INVSEEN` maintenance in `_cs_ops`, `_cs_scan` and `cmd_segments`' per-event reset. NAMED, NOT NUMBERED.
why: THE GUARD IS A RESUME POINT, AND IT CAN BE WRONG IN TWO WAYS THAT NEED DIFFERENT ROWS.
* An edit that RESTORES THE RESTART is pure cost: every verdict is right and
the walk is quadratic again. Rows 1-3 in tests/test_issue_fixes.py see it.
Measured 2026-09-13: `sudo` or `!` plus 2,642 quoted runs goes from ~4 s to
KILLED at the 60 s ceiling, and row 2's pair from ~1.4x to ~28x.
* An edit that makes the resume point WRONG changes a verdict and no cost.
ROW 0 sees it, one command per edit. Rows 1-4 cannot be relied on: on the
whitespace-dropping candidate all four stayed green.
FOUR ONE-LINE EDITS ARE NOT IN THIS SET, because no row sees them and an entry
nothing catches can only score ESCAPED. Measured 2026-09-13 on the emitted
dependency-gate, each changed no verdict on 33 probe commands, no count of the
runtime suffix pin, and no cost shape out of seven:
* scan-restart-no-pend: the `_cs_scan` restart branch, which its own comment
records as unreachable, because a quoted run cannot carry a separator.
* ops-append-pend-unguarded: the memo guard on the `_cs_ops` pend append.
The last three are FINDINGS, not proof the sites are dead: a shape that needs
them may exist, and none was found.
